You... you know that part of the story is true, right? As in, you know that Wild Bill Hickok was a real person, who was killed on that day, in that place, in that manner, by that man, in real life?

Oh my god! Mind blown.

Was Deadwood based on real characters or a part of history though?

Deadwood is very, very loosely based on real events that happened in the real town of Deadwood, in what is now South Dakota, during the mid-to-late 1870's.

As mentioned, Wild Bill was a real dude, and the details of his death in the show are more or less accurate.

Seth Bullock? Real person. Al Swearengen? Real person. Charlie Utter? Yep. Calamity Jane. Real.

The show is fiction, but its cast of characters includes some real people from a real place. Wikipedia that shit. It's worth knowing.

Also, of all the great tv shows that have come along post-Sopranos... The Wire, Breaking Bad, etc... the ones people talk about, Deadwood may very well have the absolute best writing of all of them. The dialogue is on another level, and there's nothing to compare to it, really. It's sublime poetry punctuated with profanity, and nearly every word said on the show is absolutely beautiful as literature.

If the show had had the chance to finish on its own terms, it would be remembered as being right up there in the pantheon of great shows from the last 15 years. Hell, it is anyway.

Enjoy.
